body:
Thank you all for attending the meeting today and a special thank you to Dan for taking meeting notes! Here are the notes from this meeting (the next one is at https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11258):

### Agenda  
Attendees: Luke Warlow, Joey Arhar, Panos Astithas, Kurt Catti-Schmidt, Keith Cirkel, Dan Clark, Emilio Cobos Álvarez, Mason Freed, Chris Harrelson, Hoch Hochkeppel, Brian Kardell, Alison Maher, Olli Pettay, Kagami Rosylight, Benjamin VanderSloot, Anne van Kesteren  
Scribe: Dan

1. Review past action items
    1. Luke will create a PR for [file upload control rendering should specify the button element to use](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11130) to specify that it is a button.
        1. [Done](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11257)
    1. Luke to bring his thoughts on popover source to the issue/PR 
        1. [Done](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9111#issuecomment-2812140097)
    1. Emilio will send a PR for content-visibility monkeypatch
        1. [smaug] perhaps this draft [https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11241](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11241) 
        1. [emilio] Yes, along with the linked issues and CSS spec PR
    1. Noam will discuss internally about [focus fixup timing](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11211)
        1. Done.
1. Carryovers from last time
    1. [Joey] [Popover does not know what triggered it](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9111)
        1. Will continue discussing it asynchronously.
    1. [Keith] [Dialog requestClose causes several issues with regard to interplay of CloseWatcher](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11230)
        1. Keith will record the consensus in the issue.
    1. [Kurt] [Support fragment references in the `<link>` tag's href attribute](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11019)
        1. Kurt will summarize the various options in the issue.
1. New topics
    1. [Anne] [Consider changing Response's url so it includes a fragment](https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1167)
        1. Olli will find the Gecko experts to chime in. Chris will ask Domenic for a Chromium perspective.

### Action Items

1.  @keithamus will record the consensus in the [dialog requestClose causes several issues with regard to interplay of CloseWatcher](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11230) issue.
1. @KurtCattiSchmidt will summarize the various options around [support fragment references in the `<link>` tag's href attribute](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11019) in the issue.
1. @smaug---- will find the Gecko experts to chime in on [consider changing Response's url so it includes a fragment](https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1167). @chrishtr will ask Domenic for a Chromium perspective.

### Minutes  
Scribe: Dan Clark

Luke: PR for [file upload control rendering should specify the button element to use](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11130) still in progress.

Luke: Left comments in [Done](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9111#issuecomment-2812140097), most have been answered.

Olli: PR [https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11241](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11241) is in draft state  
Panos: I'll stop tracking

Panos: Thoughts on date formatting?  
Anne: It's fine.

Panos: Noam says focus fixup timing is done, any further comments?  
[no one had comments]

**Topic:  [Popover does not know what triggered it**](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9111)  
Joey: We can keep reviewing the PR unless anyone here has thoughts?  
Panos: If no one has feedback, inclined to take it off the agenda.  
Joey: Sounds good.

**Topic:  [Dialog requestClose causes several issues with regard to interplay of CloseWatcher**](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11230)  
Keith: We spoke about this last time. There are a couple ways to solve it. There's hesitance to pick one. I'd like to get consensus here. One is to remove closewatcher mechanics from requestClose. Has small ramifications. Alternative is to add steps for insertion and removal. Need to be careful. There are cases, maybe Luke can talk to those. Hard to ensure closewatcher exists. Many ways to have a dialog, add open attribute before or after connect.  
Luke: Most of the decisions narrows down to do we want requestClose to work in terms of removing the open attribute and firing events on disconnected dialogs, or just connected ones. Previously crashed in Chrome, webkit currently fires events. Solution needs to decide between whether it does or doesn't.   
Mason: Two questions, one about closewatcher itself. Spec asserts only exists when connected to active document and open. Could roll that back, or seal up all the things that were missed, which is the case we're talking about. My weak preference is seal off what was missed, only show closewatcher when there is an active dialog waiting to be closed.  
Anne: What state gets reset when we disconnect?  
Mason: Depends. New or current? With Luke's PR, when you disconnect it cleans up closewatcher and removes dialog from Open diaglost list.  
Lukes: Also removes top layer and ismodal flag.  
Anne: If state can't change in disconnected state, doesn't make sense to fire events. What are they signaling? More sense to return early. Events are about state change.  
Luke: If you have dialog with open set on disconnected dialog and call close, it'll fire top level event and remove open attr.  
Mason: That part feels funny.  
Luke: It closes it and open attribute is removed. `.open` is false. Depends on defn of open/close  
Mason: My definition of that is, is it visible  
Anne: It's more about top layer than attribute  
Luke: dialogs don't have to be top layer, but I take your point. It's in a weird state  
Anne: If we run logic on disconnect to clear state, we should no-op the close  
Mason: [missed]  
Anne: Guessing we'll have to do an early return.  
Mason: Seems like opening methods should throw if they can't show. Closing methods (close and requestClose) shouldn't throw if the dialog is disconnected.  
Kieth: `<detail>` does not assert and does not return early. If we want to use precedent, might want to look there. For showmodal, is convincing case that top layer needs to do that stuff (assert). For requestClose and close, doesn't need to, necessarily.  
Luke: Makes sense that showModal doesn't work in disconnected dialog, can't be modal if not in document. Would be completely inert. Calling show and close and requestCLose, I know show() does some stuff but essentially comes down to does attr get removed. The fact you can do that in a disconnected dialog probably means calling show() on disconnected dialog should just do that. If we have handling for setting open to false in disconnected dialog, makes sense that calling the method could do that. If we make it so close and requestClose work in disconnected dialogs…for inactive documents, more of a case to be had for not doing anything.  
Mason: Lots of what you said boils down to open attribute is funny. We have to live with that. I don't have strong optionions on throw vs not throw. Only ones that have close watchers actually open dialogs in active documents.  
Keith: No reproducible examples, but one strange thing w/ close watchers is you can observe difference between dialog with open attribute set then inserted, vs the reverse ordering. Gets funny with close watchers. Gets funny with timing and order of operations.  
Anne: open attr is funny for `<details>` too, it's what the events key off. Don't like it as precedent.  
Mason: Follow up for Keith, in your example, I'd expect closewatcher to be created when dialog with open attribute is created, or when open attr is set to true. I think that's what spec and Chrome do. The design flaw is it has lots of cases to account for.  
Keith: if open attr is synced with closewatcher, that's ok. Becomes discrepancies where if closewatcher is not synced with `open`, and instead something else, the timing of closewatcher gets complicated. I think if we can show whenever we set `open` attr, we also need to assert closewatcher is also active, i think we want to establish closewatcher whenever `open` is set, destroy it when it's removed.  
Mason: Agree, that's what I tried to do in Chromium.  
Luke: One difference is whether it's connected has an impact. Can get in a state where you have `open` but not closewatcher. With current PR, it gets created when `open` is added rather than document insertions. If we do it so you only have closewatcher in active, connected state, with `open`, question is does requestClose work? I'm OK with it being early return, although I'd prefer it to work.  
[nodding]  
Anne: Does dialog have strong ref to closewatcher  
Luke: Depends on impl but I think yes  
Anne: In that case is preferable to sever ref asap, which is on disconnect.  
Keith: Does destroying consume a history activation?  
Luke: No  
Keith: I think it's only when you close, not on the request.  
Luke: Request to close not via JS. Eg esc key.  
Keith: Right, request to close has bool for requiring history activation. To go back, requestClose, return when it's disconnected? To establish the closewatcher on insertion steps? I think that means it's observable, if you have a disconnected dialog and set open, and call close, is that an issue?  
Luke: You have open atttr change steps too. Handles most of those cases.  
Keith: Does that mean you have closewatcher on disconnected doc when set open?  
Anne: No, returns early.  
Luke: close doesn't return early, requestClose() would (per this proposal)  
Anne: Why can't close return early?  
Keith: Close does not fire cancel steps, does not go through closewatcher flow. Dialog close just fires a close event.  
Mason: And removes open attr  
Keith: So close is potentially fine as is. Is discrepancy between close and requestClose if we return early on requestClose. Don't have strong opinions but is a little weird.  
Luke: I think close doesn't need to early return. requestClose would. Can probably change requestClose in terms of webcompat, changing close probably problematic.  
Keith: seems the direction is to return early in requstClose. But why opposition to alternative [missed; regarding closewatcher]  
Mason: Feels weird and troublesome. I was going to say, the addition of requestClose is meant to mirror the one on closeWatcher. I think the design tried to be consistent. It feels weird if there's no closewatcher why does requestClose do it?  
Keith: I agree, there's an observable difference between implementations. The closewatcher is important , but it's tautological. The important thing is requestClose has closewatcher.  
Could be surprising if there are differences in between disconnected and disconnected case.  
E.g. with tests and polyfills – with polyfill, might want to query element without connecting it.  
Mason: I want to ack my bias, if there are good dev reasons to go the other way, let's do that. But this felt like the best way to patch holes, fix crashes.  
Panos: can you summarize consensus in issue comment?  
Keith: Yes. Seems we are in agreement that throwing is the wrong solution. Whittled down to whether to return early for requestClose, or establish closewatcher on disconnected dialogs. Chromes impl is the first, spec PR is the latter. Do we change spec, or change Chrome?  
Mason: We're early enough, we can do either.  
Anne: Has domenic weighed in whether closewatcher should track invisible things?  
Luke: His pref was what chrome does now.  
Anne: That follows from closewatcher getting removed at disconnect. Wondering at that choice.  
Luke: I think his pref is what chrome has now rather than the spec PR.  
Mason: That's my understanding too.  
Keith: In comments, he says would prefer if they all threw. I'll put this in comment, we have a reasonable summary to discuss further.  
Anne: Severing strong ref sooner seems better. Don't care too strongly about how methods behave in response to that.

**Topic: [Support fragment references in the `<link>` tag's href attribute**](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11019)  
Kurt: Been trying to get discussion going on this. It's a known problem, sharing styles between shadows. This solution seems simpler. No external file needed, access style tag's ID ref. Also is easy to polyfill. I have an explainer, and a PR, it's stage 1, would like stage 2.  
Panos: Any feedback?  
Luke: I remember we discussed before; might want to link to other `<link>` element, do not just inline.  
Kurt: Can't do that now, but open to adding that. But what situation does it help with? Conceptually makes sense, but if style tag is in scope too, does that unlock new scenarios? Maybe if media elements don't match?  
Luke: In my head, maybe perf stuff, but maybe that's not the case?  
Anne: I continue to not be a big fan of mixing URLS and IDRefs in same value space. The idref stuff will only work in the same doc. Can't link to other doc. So already weirdness there. More weirdness with `<base>` element. Get weird thing that css has, but no concept of that in HTML; it's either url or idref. Can maybe invent that, but have to parse URL things a bit differently. Not great.  
Kurt: The URl will have the frag identifier, like an anchor. Already rules for parsing that.  
Anne: But you'd expect it to also work if url isn't pointing to the same doc. Your thing is only same doc. Which isn't true if you have pushState, have to track original URL. There are weird cases that may not be well defined.  
Kurt: Good examples, hadn't thought about pushstate or base element. Seems like those could be incorporated. Say it's only for local files for shadow DOM scenario. That's the key use cases. If they are in other documents, you don't want to use this. Ignoring thighs like base could make sense with this.  
Chris: Clarifying question about what Anne said. If you have a doc, and a fragment only anchor link, and pushstate, the anchor link won't work anymore?  
Anne: That works. But if you're at foo, and base points to slash, the fragment goes to /whatever-the-fragment-is.  
Chris: So frag anchor list with base pointing at something else is not necessarily same doc?  
Anne: Not sure how pushstate case works. If you're on /foo, and have frag link at /foo#something, and pushtate to /bar, guessing link goes to /foo. Maybe gets parsed a click time? Not sure.  
Kurt: This is an interesting case, will incorporate it in the explainer. But people using this feature won't be blocked by this.  
Anne: I consider it blocking feedback.  
Chris: I think he's saying new thing should integrate with existing  algos.  
Anne: Yeah, and we do want to have something that's intuitive and works well in these scenarios. Maybe we need to invent something like what CSS has. They recognize that if something starts with ‘#', you parse it separately, and the data structure is struct, has URL or standalone fragment, and what you end up resolving is the appropriate thing based on that. Still can be odd because href getter might not do what you expect.  
Anne: From webkits perspective we should fix that before next stage  
Kurt: Specify how it behaves? Or does this block the proposal?  
Anne: Not sure what it looks like, maybe have dedicated attr, or introduce URL and fragment concept that you shoehorn through the various things. Not sure if dedicated attr is the best option. There's at least one feature introduced in the last 6 months that did something like that  
Dan: Can you say what feature that is?  
Chris: The document render blocking features, where you can say we block rendering until certain element is parsed.  
Olli: Maybe that has the same bug  
Chris: It's an ID, not a url.  
Anne: Is it Href or IDref?  
Chris: have to check  
Anne: We discussed that before, Noam said we have it with `<link rel=expect>`.  
Olli: Should we fix that too?  
Anne: I think so.  
Panos: Kurt do you have enough to make progress?  
Kurt: Yep, I will update the explainer, come back for more feedback.

**Topic:  [Consider changing Response's url so it includes a fragment**](https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1167)  
Anne: Idea here was we want to make fragment id of response available to serviceworkers so they can do something with it before handing response to document. Could make the serviceworker support the svg view box stuff, for instance.An idea we had was to make it part of the url. That's where we store behind the scenes, but it's serialized without the fragment. But we should just expose it with hash on the response instead. It's safest, what we do today. And makes more sense from http perspective. Question is, is there implementer interest?  
Panos: Do we have the right people from Chromium and Gecko?  
Anne: Can ping people, response in next month would be nice  
Panos: Olli can you find the Gecko person?  
Olli: Yep  
Chris: This is exposing to ServiceWorkers specifically?  
Anne: More, anything that gets a response. Also fetch.  
Chris: I'll ask domenic.  
Panos: Anything else Anne?  
Anne: That's it.  
Anne: We are exposing the URL already.  
Luke: Don't we expose as string, not obj?  
Anne: Don't want to expose Url object. It's immutable. Try not to have those as return vals. Only really want to expose hash. The other info is in URL getter. If you want specific part that's not a hash, want to take response URL and put it in URL constructor.
